sources.title: An 8-Stage Model for Evaluating the Tennis Serve: Implications for Performance Enhancement and Injury Prevention
usedFor: Preparation, acceleration, and follow-through phase organization

sources.title: Kinematics characteristics of key point of interest during tennis serve among tennis players: a systematic review and meta-analysis
usedFor: Consensus event vocabulary: ball release, trophy position, racket low point, and ball impact
Explicit warning that joint-angle definitions vary between studies

sources.title: The expert eye? An inter-rater comparison of elite tennis serve kinematics and performance
usedFor: Evidence that trained observers can reach strong agreement on broad 2D serve features such as rhythm, trunk action, and leg drive
Caution that fine rotational judgments such as shoulder internal-rotation speed are less reliably rated from 2D replay

sources.title: Kinematics of the Tennis Serve Using an Optoelectronic Motion Capture System: Are There Correlations between Joint Angles and Racket Velocity?
usedFor: Broad trophy-position and impact elbow-angle plausibility ranges
Separation of trophy position, racket low point, and ball impact

sources.title: The Influence of Kinematics on Tennis Serve Speed: An In-Depth Analysis Using Xsens MVN Biomech Link Technology
usedFor: Observable loading, cocking, impact, and follow-through event ordering
Caution that serve-event characterization still lacks complete consensus

sources.title: Tennis Player Actions Dataset for Human Pose Estimation
usedFor: 500 sequential serve frames with COCO/OpenPose-style body keypoints
Research-only pose and temporal weak supervision

observable: body-center position relative to the visible feet
notObservable: Exact 3D shoulder, pelvis, or trunk rotation
